newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Basques agree to back conservative budget.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Basques agree to back conservative budget.

text.p: Spain's moderate Basque Nationalist Party (PNV) has agreed with the ruling conservatives to back the draft 1997 budget in exchange for regional tax concessions, a PNV spokesman said on Wednesday.
The budget is already guaranteed a safe passage on the combined votes of the ruling conservatives, their Catalan nationalist allies and the Canary Islands coalition.

Deputy Basque President Juan Jose Ibarretxe and Secretary of State for the Exchequer Juan Costa struck a deal early on Wednesday for the PNV's support for the 1997 draft in a three-day debate which began on Tuesday, PNV parliamentary spokesman Inaki Anasagasti said.
Parliament will vote on the budget on November 22.

Although their five votes are technically superfluous, they would give the ruling Popular Party (PP) a comfortable margin over the Socialists and the Communists who have introduced motions rejecting the budget.
The contents of the tax deal are based on concessions the PP promised the PNV in exchange for backing the investiture of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar in May.
Among the measures agreed are greater control over some types of tax revenues such as special taxes on alcohol, tobacco and fossil fuels as well as non-residents' tax.
